claims.statement: The EU Medical Device Regulation requires each manufacturer to establish and update a post-market surveillance system that actively and systematically gathers and analyses quality, performance and safety data throughout a device's lifetime.
MDR post-market clinical follow-up is a continuing process for updating clinical evaluation and can include suitable registries or PMCF studies under a documented plan.

Hypothesis: reserved Polish clinic capacity and biosignal expertise can deliver accepted evidence at attractive cost; sponsor demand, study classification and notified-body acceptance are unvalidated.

contrary_evidence: MDR requires thorough, objective clinical evaluation and protection of subjects; contractual clinic access cannot substitute for scientific, ethical or regulatory adequacy.
For some devices and claims, formal clinical investigations and sponsor obligations may exceed the proposed bootstrap scope.

economics.acquisition_route: Contract one clinic and one regulatory specialist for a clearly classified service, then sell a paid feasibility or non-interventional pilot to one device sponsor before building a participant panel.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated path: 50 annual projects and retainers averaging PLN 100,000 would yield PLN 5m revenue; at 30% operating profit and a 5x value, a 75% founder stake would be about PLN 5.6m. A 7-9 year route requires audit-ready quality systems and repeat sponsors, with no value assigned to patient data itself.
economics.founder_time: 15-20 hours per week for protocol design, data QA and sponsor communication; medical oversight, ethics submissions and participant care stay with qualified professionals.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated estimate: 35-55% after clinic, clinician, recruitment, monitoring, insurance and regulatory-specialist costs; margins improve only through repeatable protocols, not weaker oversight.
economics.payback: Unvalidated target: 18-30 months after six to ten paid evidence packages; regulatory delays can extend this materially.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated hypothesis: PLN 35,000-120,000 for a bounded observational evidence package and PLN 20,000-60,000 annual PMCF or post-market operations retainer; clinical investigations may cost more and are outside the first pilot.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Manufacturers have continuing post-market duties and may renew annual evidence work; every new intended purpose or device still requires fresh scope and permissions.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: validated clinic workflows, recruitment reliability and reusable non-personal operating templates shorten future studies while sponsor data remains segregated
fingerprint.customer: European digital-health, wearable and biosignal-device manufacturers needing clinical evaluation, usability, post-market surveillance or PMCF evidence
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: regulatory consultants and notified-body-adjacent advisers refer sponsors; the founder targets biosignal and wearable niches where technical credibility is strongest
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: protocol operations, clinic capacity, participant logistics, instrumented data capture and reproducible analysis sold per project plus annual post-market evidence retainers
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: the device sponsor pays a study setup fee, per-completed-participant fee and final evidence-package fee at predefined quality milestones
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a conformity milestone, notified-body question, post-market plan, new claim, market expansion or an evidence gap in a defined user group

founder_fit: Strong match to neuroscience, EEG/biosignal, data-science and health interests.
A medical-student partner can improve domain understanding but does not replace licensed oversight.
Project delivery can be analytical and systems-led, with recruitment delegated to clinics.
The founder can focus on a narrow technical niche rather than public-facing health content.
risks: Incorrectly classifying a study or mishandling consent can invalidate evidence and create serious legal exposure.
Health data is sensitive, breach impact is high and reuse is tightly limited.
Sponsors may require accredited CRO capabilities, insurance or quality systems beyond a bootstrap studio.
Recruitment delay and protocol deviation can destroy margins.

structure.control_point: reserved clinic recruitment and measurement capacity combined with protocol-specific, purpose-limited participant data permissions
structure.critical_dependency: the medical partner, ethics and data-protection pathway must be valid and sponsors or notified bodies must accept the resulting methods and evidence

thesis: Create a Polish evidence-operations studio for EU wearable, biosignal and lower-risk medical-device companies by contracting reserved recruitment and measurement windows with clinics and laboratories. Each engagement uses sponsor-specific protocols, ethics and data-protection review, participant consent and purpose-limited data-use terms; the company sells a quality-controlled evidence package and workflow, not a reusable patient-data pool. Begin with non-interventional post-market follow-up or usability work only after regulatory counsel confirms the study category.
title: Clinic-Access Foundry for Device Evidence
uncertainties: Which study class can be delivered lawfully with a clinic partner and within PLN 85,000 startup capital?
Will sponsors accept a Polish boutique operator for bounded PMCF or usability work?
What clinic capacity can be reserved without minimum-volume guarantees?
Which biosignal niche has repeat protocols and enough sponsor density?
